title: The Delivery Backlog
briefing: The earlier bottled-water delivery strategy has left distribution depots full of empty containers and tanker queues. Essential deliveries continue, but a cleanup contract would displace the vehicles and funds that brought emergency supply into the neighborhoods.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Refill stations need pressure tests before use; opening all of them today would risk contaminating clean hoses.
private_intelligence.community: Community volunteers can manage a deposit return, but residents without spare cash would need a deposit waiver.
private_intelligence.economy: A packaging buyer offers revenue for sorted material, provided collection vehicles deliver it outside normal shifts.
private_intelligence.safety: Container piles block emergency access to two depots; clearing those routes is more urgent than reaching a recycling target.

choices.title: Sell and Sort Locally
choices.description: Pay neighborhood teams to sort containers for commercial recovery.
choices.consequence: Sorting creates local income and keeps water deliveries moving, but blocked depots clear slowly and supervision is uneven.

choices.title: Clear Depots Centrally
choices.description: Hire an emergency collection fleet and keep sealed-water deliveries.
choices.consequence: Depot access improves quickly, but the costly parallel supply and waste routes strain the maintenance budget.

choices.title: Build a Refill Network
choices.description: Test neighborhood refill points and waive deposits where needed.
choices.consequence: Local refill access restores confidence and reduces material use, while testing and new routing slow immediate delivery.
